rule: Conditional compilation sits in a cfg_if::cfg_if! block, an enclosing platform module or a braced block, never as a #[cfg(...)] or a conditional #[cfg_attr(...)] directly on an import, another unbraced declaration or an unbraced statement (root AGENTS.md, 'Explicit scope for control flow and conditional compilation'; GwzCoreSessionPlan CS1.7). check_cfg_boundaries.py's docstring defines the terms. This list is the complete inventory of the occurrences that predate the check, taken from the HEAD blobs of gwz-core bd538656, gwz-cli ebbea902 and gwz-py 0b535dc5: unbraced items (use, mod name;, a fn without a body, type, const, static, a unit or tuple struct, a macro item) and unbraced statements (let, an expression statement, a statement macro). Each is migration debt that CS1.7 records and does not migrate (GwzCoreSessionPlan §1.3). Fields, variants, match arms and parameters are out of scope and not listed, because they are neither items nor statements and Rust gives them no explicit boundary: at those HEADs conditional attributes sit on 31 fields and variants, 7 struct-expression fields, 8 match arms, and 2 parameters and 2 call arguments; 4 more sit on tail expressions, which have no ';' and are not statements. An entry is keyed by repository, file, conditional attributes and target, never by line: the whole rendered text of a use item, a macro item or an expression statement, 'let' with the pattern of a let, and the kind and name of any other item. count is the number of identical occurrences in the file. check_cfg_boundaries.py fails on an unlisted occurrence, a modified listed one included, and on an entry that no longer matches. Its --shrink-from mode, which the checked-artifact boundary job runs against the pull request's base and the pushed-over commit, fails on an added occurrence (a count, summed over files, above the base's) or a narrowed scope (a repository dropped or moved, or a base root no longer covered), so the list only shrinks: remove an entry, or lower its count, in the change that removes the occurrence. It passes a change that removes a listed occurrence in one file and adds an identical one elsewhere in the same repository, because a movement-only split cannot be told apart from remove-and-recreate; review reads an allowlist path change as a move claim to verify. scripts/run_tests.py runs the check over all three repositories and fails when gwz-cli or gwz-py is not checked out beside gwz-core, unless a CI job without them passes --skip-cfg-siblings. No CI job checks gwz-cli or gwz-py yet, so their coverage is local-only (run_tests.py in a workspace) until their own CI runs the check, a follow-up once CS1.7 is on gwz-core's main.
